text: Yes, the 2022 loss was detected using Sentinel-2 imagery. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which incorporates Sentinel-2 data, identified a 0.6-hectare tree-cover loss event in 2022. This event met the corroboration rule, as the JRC 2020 reference confirmed the area was forested in 2020. The loss was further validated by the MGAP forest map, which classified the area as native forest. While some smaller patches (0.2 ha) were excluded due to size, the primary 2022 loss was confirmed by Sentinel-2 observations.
